articles.title: Prosecutors target Sept. 9 to wrap up Duterte confi, intel fund case
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — The House of Representatives prosecution panel is targeting Sept. 9 to complete its presentation of evidence in the impeachment case against Vice President Sara Duterte over her…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — The House of Representatives prosecution panel is targeting Sept. 9 to complete its presentation of evidence in the impeachment case against Vice President Sara Duterte over her alleged misuse of confidential funds, even as prosecutors have yet to finalize their list of witnesses.
House prosecutor and Bicol Saro party-list Rep. Terry Ridon said that the date announced by lead prosecutor Rep. Gerville Luistro remained a working target rather than a firm deadline.
“The Sept. 9 date that has been mentioned remains a target,” Ridon said at a House press conference Thursday. He described Sept. 9 as an optimistic target for completing the presentation of evidence.

The prosecution is presenting evidence under Article I, which covers P500 million in confidential funds spent by the Office of the Vice President (OVP) from December 2022 to the third quarter of 2023 and P112.5 million released to the Department of Education in 2023 while Duterte headed the agency.
Ridon said the length of cross-examinations and questions from senator-judges could still affect the timetable.
“We cannot control several things — the cross and the questions of the senator-judges,” he said. “But we will try to wrap up by that date,” he added.

Asked whether the prosecution still intended to present Ramil Madriaga and the purported confidential fund recipient identified in documents as Mary Grace Piatos, Ridon said the panel would disclose its final lineup as it approached the close of Article I.
“Let’s just wait and see what the final list of those who will testify at the trial will be,” he said.
Ridon said the prosecution’s immediate priority was establishing the connection between the handling of the confidential funds and Duterte’s instructions or official actions.
“The important aspect is really proving the tie to the vice president,” he said.
He cited the testimony of former OVP special disbursing officer Gina Acosta, OVP Assistant Secretary Lemuel Ortonio and former Department of Education chief of staff Atty. Michael Poa.

Acosta testified that Duterte instructed her to turn over OVP confidential-fund cash to security officer Col. Raymund Dante Lachica. Ortonio and Poa testified about their respective official roles and the limits of their knowledge of the transactions.
Ridon said those accounts had already supplied the evidence the prosecution considered central to linking the challenged transactions to Duterte.
“That was already mentioned in the testimonies of Ms. Acosta, Mr. Ortonio and Atty. Poa,” he said.
The panel will decide whether additional witnesses are necessary after the remaining scheduled testimony and questioning, Ridon said.
“All the others will just serve as additional evidence to the overall effort to prove this article of impeachment,” the lawmaker added. “That part is already done.”

articles.title: Leptospirosis cases reach 6,253; DOH warns of post-flood surge
articles.summary: Leptospirosis cases in the country have reached 6,253 from Jan. 4 to Aug. 29, the Department of Health (DOH) said yesterday, warning that infections may surge as another wave of cases could be…

blocks.text: September 4, 2026 | 12:00am
Residents wade through floodwaters along Zapote Junction in Las Piñas on August 29, 2026.
Edd Gumban / The Philippine STAR

MANILA, Philippines — Leptospirosis cases in the country have reached 6,253 from Jan. 4 to Aug. 29, the Department of Health (DOH) said yesterday, warning that infections may surge as another wave of cases could be experienced in two weeks due to the disease’s incubation period.
Of the cases logged so far, 378 deaths were recorded with a case fatality rate of 6.05 percent.
DOH Undersecretary Gloria Balboa said that the recent figure is lower by 12 percent compared to the data from the same period last year.
In Metro Manila, 72 percent of leptospirosis cases were from flood-related exposure, with unemployed or informal workers making up 55 percent of all infections.

“They are the ones who need to work daily. They may not like to wade through floodwaters, but they had to do so to provide food for their family,” Balboa explained, as she appealed to employers to provide personal protective gear as part of occupational health and welfare for the workers.

According to Balboa, several leptospirosis beds have reached almost full capacity in East Avenue Medical Center and the National Kidney and Transplant Institute in Quezon City and José R. Reyes Memorial Medical Center and San Lazaro Hospital in Manila.

In Quezon City, hospitals have already reached over 400 cases, with more than half reported just last month. Data released by the QC Epidemiology and Surveillance Division (QCESD) on Wednesday showed that a total of 437 leptospirosis cases have been reported from Jan. 1 to Aug. 28.
Although the figure is lower by 18 percent from the same period last year, the QCESD said more than half of the cases or a total of 296 were reported from Aug. 1 to 28.
Ten of 30 deaths reported in the city also occurred during the same period. Some 171 cases were reported between Aug. 16 to 22, which QCESD said breached the “epidemic threshold.”

Leptospirosis is caused by the bacteria leptospira, which can spread through direct contact with the urine of infected animals such as rats and pigs, or with a urine-contaminated environment such as floodwaters.
MMDA: 662 floodings recorded in NCR
The Metropolitan Manila Development Authority (MMDA) has recorded 662 flooding incidents in the National Capital Region (NCR) since the start of 2026.
According to data presented by the Flood Control and Sewerage Management Office, 58 percent of the flooding incidents were recorded in Quezon City, with 246 reports, and in Manila with 140 reports.?

“These two local government units alone account for a significant portion of the total reported flooding incidents,” the office said.?MMDA said other areas with relatively high numbers of incidents include Mandaluyong with 62, Malabon with 57 and Valenzuela with 56 flood reports.?In the month of August alone, the MMDA said 405 floods were reported.
“While shallow flooding makes up a large portion of the reported incidents, there are specific locations where flood depths reach mean tire or even waist-level,” the agency said.
It added that these areas require more drainage improvement, flood control interventions and emergency preparedness.? – Rhodina Villanueva, Janvic Mateo

articles.title: Local execs vow proper use of P58.32- billion LGSF
articles.summary: Learning a hard lesson from massive anomalies in the flood control scandal, the League of Municipalities in the Philippines gave assurances that the government’s record high P58.32-billion…

blocks.text: Headlines
September 4, 2026 | 12:00am

“We will not fail the President. We will make sure that the funds are spent wisely based on the Department of Budget and Management’s guidelines and subject to strict auditing and accountability rules,” LMP president Faustino “Inno” Dy V promised.
STAR / File

MANILA, Philippines — Learning a hard lesson from massive anomalies in the flood control scandal, the League of Municipalities in the Philippines gave assurances that the government’s record high P58.32-billion budget for local government units in 2027 will be used properly.
He said there are “strict safeguards” in place to keep the proposed P58.32-billion Local Government Support Fund (LGSF) for 2027 “free from political favoritism and ensure LGUs get their fair share.”
Budget watchdogs have warned that the LGSF is a lump-sum appropriation that smacks of a form of pork barrel.

The proposed LGSF includes P37.49 billion in financial assistance to LGUs, P10.3 billion for the Growth Equity Fund, P9.74 billion for the Barangay Development Program of the National Task Force to End Local Communist Armed Conflict, and P1 billion for support and assistance under participatory budgeting.

LGUs will receive these funds on top of their National Tax Allotment, formerly known as the Internal Revenue Allotment before the Supreme Court’s Mandanas-Garcia ruling expanded the tax base used to compute the share of local governments.

The country’s 1,491 municipalities will receive the largest combined NTA allocation at P448.70 billion. Another P303.56 billion will go to 83 provinces, P303.56 billion to 149 cities and P263.97 billion to 41,912 barangays.

“Guard rails have been put in place by the DBM to ensure the equitable and proportionate distribution of the LGSF among all provincial, city and municipal governments, in keeping with the directive of the President,” Dy stressed.
Release of such funds to LGUs, according to President Marcos, “should be free from partisan interests.”

“The record LGSF allocation shows President Marcos’ trust and confidence in local governments, from provinces and cities to municipalities and barangays. It also reflects his commitment to giving LGUs more room and resources to drive local development,” said Dy, mayor of Echague town in Isabela and son of Speaker Faustino Dy III.
Executive Secretary Ralph Recto said that the LGSF for 2027 is the highest in the country’s history.
In a statement, Dy described the LGSF as an equity tool that helps ensure a fairer distribution of national resources among LGUs and “limits the space for patronage politics.”

Among the programs funded through LGSF is the distribution of 10 kilos of free rice every two months to nearly eight million families. It may also be used for farm-to-market roads, water systems, health facilities and multipurpose buildings that can serve as evacuation centers. during disasters.

articles.title: Lacson, Cayetano trade barbs anew
articles.summary: Senators Panfilo Lacson and Alan Peter Cayetano renewed their trading of barbs over allegations of anomalous flood control and land reclamation projects in Taguig, Cayetano’s bailiwick.

blocks.text: September 4, 2026 | 12:00am
Senator Panfilo “Ping” Lacson at Sen. Alan Peter Cayetano
STAR / Ryan Baldemor

MANILA, Philippines — Senators Panfilo Lacson and Alan Peter Cayetano renewed their trading of barbs over allegations of anomalous flood control and land reclamation projects in Taguig, Cayetano’s bailiwick.

Cayetano went on Facebook Live on Wednesday to accuse Lacson of being behind a “demolition job” against him when Lacson alleged that Cayetano has control over Taguig’s allegedly anomalous public works.
Ang laki na po ng ginanda ngayon ng siyudad ng Taguig. That’s why it’s very unfair na nasa-subject ito sa isang demolition job, isang witch hunt, at saka isang trial by publicity,” Cayetano said.
Cayetano said Lacson is going on a “witch hunt” to “confuse” the people about Taguig’s development.

“Yes, tahasang ko pong sinasabi na si Senator Panfilo Lacson ay gumagawa ng isang demolition job, ng isang trial by publicity, at isa pong witch hunt sa siyudad ng Taguig. Wala pong problema na ako akusahan niya, public official po ako, pero po i-link niya sa Taguig at sa akin lahat ng projects, lahat na po ng titulo doon, it’s not only po unfair, but simple lang eh, if he cannot convince people, he will try to confuse people,” Cayetano said.
Lacson responded the next day by saying that the evidence gathered on Taguig is making Cayetano “quake while quacking.”

“Sen. Cayetano can accuse me all he wants of ‘politically motivated’ witch-hunt, fake news and trial by publicity, but I’m sure, he quakes in his shoes each time he sees every piece of evidence that I present each time he resorts to his trademark ‘quack-quack’ on Facebook Live,” Lacson said.

articles.title: SWS: 33% of Pinoys say quality of life improved
articles.summary: One in every three Filipinos reported experiencing better quality of life in the past 12 months, an improvement compared to data from the first quarter of the year, according to the latest survey by…

blocks.text: September 4, 2026 | 12:00am
Photo shows Filipinos celebrating in a feast.
AFP / File

MANILA, Philippines — One in every three Filipinos reported experiencing better quality of life in the past 12 months, an improvement compared to data from the first quarter of the year, according to the latest survey by Social Weather Stations (SWS).
The survey, conducted from June 20 to 29, showed that 33 percent of respondents said their quality of life had improved over the past year.
It was up 10 points from the 23 percent obtained in a similar survey in March 2026.
Thirty-three percent said their quality of life worsened, down from 50 percent, while respondents whose quality of life stayed the same increased from 26 percent to 34 percent.
The latest poll resulted in a net gainers score of zero, up from -26 in the March poll.
The “net gainers” score is the rounded off difference of those who said their lives improved from those who said their lives worsened.
The latest score reversed the downward trend that began in the third quarter of 2025. It was still below the +12 obtained in June 2025.

articles.title: DBM OKs P8.68 billion for teachers’ pay raise
articles.summary: Salary upgrades for 93,344 public school personnel are underway after the Department of Budget and Management (DBM) approved the release of an additional P8.68 billion to the Department of Education.

blocks.text: September 4, 2026 | 12:00am
Qualified personnel’s positions have been reclassified under the Expanded Career Progression (ECP) System.
Google Map

MANILA, Philippines — Salary upgrades for 93,344 public school personnel are underway after the Department of Budget and Management (DBM) approved the release of an additional P8.68 billion to the Department of Education (DepEd).

“As teachers advance in their profession, their salaries should also increase. They have worked hard for this career advancement, so they should feel its benefits,” acting Budget Secretary Kim Robert de Leon said.
Covered by the release are fiscal years 2025 and 2026’s implementation requirements for personnel with issued notices of organization, staffing and compensation action and appointments, the DBM said.
The amount will be charged against the DepEd’s built-in personnel services lump-sum appropriations for 2026, consistent with the DBM-approved funding strategy for the ECP program.
Regional offices of the DepEd will facilitate fund releases, ensuring that the fund reaches regions where qualified personnel are assigned.
Meanwhile, the Marcos administration is proposing a sharp increase in funding for the career advancement of public school teachers next year, under the 2027 National Expenditure Program.

Under the executive-level budget, P12.09 billion has been allocated for the ECP System, up by P5.94 billion from this year’s funding to support the continued reclassification and career advancement of public school teachers.
P30 billion more sought for DOTr
Cagayan de Oro Rep. Rufus Rodriguez is pushing for an additional P30 billion to the Department of Transportation (DOTr)’s proposed P300.96 billion budget for 2027.
Additional funds would cover critical projects, including the construction of the Mindanao railway project, Rodriguez said.

Transportation Secretary Giovanni Lopez said the DOTr will look for partner countries and multilateral development partners to fund the project as the railway is in the process of beginning its feasibility study.— Josiah Antonio

articles.title: Senate ratings down, House up in Q2 – OCTA poll
articles.summary: The Senate has retained better performance and trust ratings than the House of Representatives despite a drop in the latest survey conducted by the OCTA Research group.

blocks.text: September 4, 2026 | 12:00am
Facade of the House of Representatives at the Batasan Complex in Quezon City.
The STAR / Michael Varcas, File photo
MANILA, Philippines —The Senate has retained better performance and trust ratings than the House of Representatives despite a drop in the latest survey conducted by the OCTA Research group.
From 44 percent in March, trust in the Senate dropped to 41 percent in the survey conducted from July 4 to 11.
Twenty-seven percent said they distrust the upper chamber, up from 24 percent, while undecided respondents remained at 32 percent.
The Senate’s performance rating also dropped from 42 percent to 38 percent, with those dissatisfied with its performance increasing from 27 percent to 32 percent.
Undecided respondents hardly moved, from 31 percent to 30 percent.
The latest OCTA poll coincided with the start of the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte, which started on July 6.

It also captured the tumultuous period that involved leadership changes, a shooting incident and the arrest of Senators Jinggoy Estrada and Rodante Marcoleta due to cases filed before the Sandiganbayan.
Sen. Ronald dela Rosa, who briefly appeared in May, is again in hiding due to an arrest warrant issued by the International Criminal Court.
Meanwhile, the ratings of the House of Representatives slightly improved in the second quarter, although these remain lower than the ratings of its counterpart in the upper chamber.
Thirty-eight percent said they trust the House, up from 36 percent, while 28 percent said they distrust it, down from 33 percent. Undecided respondents increased from 30 percent to 33 percent.

In terms of performance, 37 percent said they were satisfied with the lower chamber, up from 35 percent, while 32 percent were undecided, down from 35 percent. Those who were undecided hardly moved, from 30 percent to 31 percent.
OCTA’s second quarter survey had 1,200 respondents and a margin of error of plus/minus three percent.

Senior Deputy Speaker Ferdinand Hernandez said the favorable ratings of the chamber were due to its “steady focus on legislation and service” under the leadership of Speaker Faustino Dy. – Delon Porcalla

articles.title: Remulla: Judiciary needs ‘soul-searching’
articles.summary: Ombudsman Jesus Crispin Remulla yesterday urged the judiciary to undertake “soul-searching” as he lamented the dismissal of corruption cases filed before the courts.

blocks.text: September 4, 2026 | 12:00am
Ombudsman Jesus Crispin Remulla speaks during a briefing on his office’s pro- posed 2027 budget, at the Senate yesterday.
Ryan Baldemor
MANILA, Philippines — Ombudsman Jesus Crispin Remulla yesterday urged the judiciary to undertake “soul-searching” as he lamented the dismissal of corruption cases filed before the courts.
During the briefing of the proposed P7.232-billion Office of the Ombudsman budget for 2027, Remulla told senators that “the judiciary has to be examined closely by everybody.”
“They themselves should go soul-searching, so we can be a better country,” Remulla said.

He lamented that there were corruption cases filed before the Sandiganbayan that had been pending for 15 years, resulting in their dismissal for inordinate delay. He also cited the reversal of case decisions by the Court of Appeals, which Remulla said “came out of nowhere” and is “discouraging” to investigators.
He said he discussed this “worrying trend” with Supreme Court (SC) Senior Associate Justice Marvic Leonen.
Not aspiring for CJ
Remulla also dismissed reports that he was among those aspiring to become the chief justice when Alexander Gesmundo retires in November.
“I have no more aspirations, this is the job I want to be able to finish,” Remulla said, telling reporters that he is “not applying” for the SC post.
Remulla was appointed ombudsman in October 2025 and will serve until 2032.
He stressed that eliminating corruption can help the government reduce poverty by ensuring there are more funds to help vulnerable sectors.
Senators have assured Remulla that they would augment the ombudsman’s budget to help with its anticorruption mandate, as he defended the request for P51.47 million in confidential funds.

Sen. JV Ejercito said that while his committee cannot promise to restore the ombudsman’s originally proposed P148 million confidential funds, “we might add a little, especially after hearing what programs and investigations could be affected.” – Daphne Galvez

articles.title: Palace eyes integration of flood master plan
articles.summary: The Marcos administration is considering integrating the flood control master plan drawn during the term of the late president Benigno Aquino III with other frameworks to come up with a system that…

blocks.text: September 4, 2026 | 12:00am

President Marcos, along with Public Works Secretary Vince Dizon, inspects the newly rehabilitated drainage system along G. Araneta Avenue in Quezon City yesterday. The work is part of the drainage improvement project in the city and the national government’s intensified flood mitigation efforts under ‘Oplan Kontra Baha.’
STAR / File

MANILA, Philippines —The Marcos administration is considering integrating the flood control master plan drawn during the term of the late president Benigno Aquino III with other frameworks to come up with a system that addresses the new realities caused by climate change.
Palace press officer Claire Castro said flood mitigation master plans were crafted in the 1930s and 1940s, but were not implemented in the previous decades.
Castro said the government already has plans for major river basins aimed at preventing excessive water flow during a cyclone.

“(Department of Public Works and Highways) Secretary Vince Dizon mentioned the Aquino-Singson master plan and it is one (of the frameworks) that may be studied,” Castro said in a press briefing yesterday, referring to the plan the DPWH formulated under its former chief Rogelio Singson and approved by Aquino in 2012.
Singson had said that the framework could only be carried out fully by 2035 as it involves large-scale infrastructure projects.

“So these will be integrated and there is a need to update them. During a previous meeting, the President cited the need to update the measures that have to be undertaken because of the possible effects of climate change. The plans before may no longer be attuned with the effect of climate change,” Castro said.

In 2024, President Marcos ordered the DPWH,the environment department and other agencies to revise the flood control master plan, saying existing measures may no longer be sufficient because of the high volume of rains.

During his visit to Tarlac on Wednesday, Marcos said the Philippines has only started implementing a flood master plan, acknowledging that it has been existing for decades, but nothing was done to enforce it.
Castro said the Aquino-Singson master plan was transmitted to the administration of former president Rodrigo Duterte.

However, Marcos’ former public works secretary Manuel Bonoan claimed to have not received any master plan, she added. “So, Secretary Vince Dizon, when he was appointed, responded to the matters related to major river basins. Now, he is coordinating on the Aquino-Singson master plan,” Castro said.

The Philippine Space Agency or PhilSA said yesterday that artificial intelligence and radar satellite imagery have mapped the floods brought by the southwest monsoon to have covered vast sections of the seven major regions of Luzon.

To keep people from living in flood-prone and other hazardous areas, Philippine National Police chief Gen. Jose Melencio Nartatez Jr. yesterday said the PNP is backing Marcos’ order to strictly enforce no-build zones in areas considered dangerous for communities.

Environment Secretary Juan Miguel Cuna ordered an intensified use of science and technology in forest and watershed protection, as he directed department field offices and enforcement units to strengthen monitoring, risk assessment and law enforcement, detect threats early and reduce risks to downstream communities. – Rainier Allan Ronda, Emmanuel Tupas, Josiah Antonio

articles.title: Around 2,000 fall ill in Indonesia after eating free school meals
articles.summary: Authorities are investigating several suspected outbreaks amid growing criticism of the scheme.

blocks.text: Around 2,000 students and teachers across Indonesia have fallen ill with food poisoning over the past three days linked to the government's free school meals programme.
In the latest case, 777 people became unwell after consuming the food at a high school in Rembang, Central Java, the institution's headteacher said.
The meals were provided through a multibillion-dollar scheme that is one of President Prabowo Subianto's signature policies, aiming to improve nutrition for Indonesia's schoolchildren.
But, as well as being the suspected source of a string of mass food poisonings, the programme has been dogged by allegations of corruption and criticism of its cost.

A total of 752 students and 25 teachers experienced symptoms of food poisoning after eating meals provided through the Makan Bergizi Gratis (MBG) programme at the high school in Lasem on Wednesday lunchtime.
"They had diarrhoea and took turns using the toilet," headteacher Juhartutik told BBC News Indonesia. "There are 40 toilets in total, so they can't accommodate everyone."
The school has since sent nearly 1,200 pupils and 95 members of staff home, while several were taken to hospital.
Juhartutik said the government would cover any medical costs and that the local food distributor had come to the school to "take responsibility".
The suspected outbreak came after 730 people fell ill after consuming MBG meals at an Islamic boarding school in Sidoarjo, East Java, on Tuesday, a local health official said.
Reni said their child felt dizzy and nauseous before developing stomach problems after eating the meal.
Some of those affected required hospital treatment, with some students being transported in wheelchairs because they were too weak to stand.
Hundreds of others have been affected by suspected cases of food poisoning linked to the free school meals this week, including hundreds across several schools in Tana Toraja, South Sulawesi.
Improper storage or poorly prepared food are often to blame for cases of food poisoning, in which the body rejects the contaminated food.
Parents and teachers have told reporters of slimy chicken, as well as food that appeared undercooked and had a fishy odour.
Local authorities are investigating the cause of the suspected outbreaks, with food samples being tested for possible contamination.
The head of the food distribution unit in Lasem, Achmad Sholeh Syarifudin, apologised and took "full responsibility for the recovery of students and teachers".
He said the unit would conduct a comprehensive evaluation of its operation following the incident.
The head of Indonesia's National Nutrition Agency has said: "If it is identified that there was negligence and there are criminal elements, I apologise, we cannot help."

articles.title: Norway seizes Russian ship in Svalbard to compensate Ukraine
articles.summary: Authorities in Norway have seized a Russian ship, the Professor Molchanov, on a court order sought and obtained by Naftogaz in Ukraine. Russia has protested the move, which stems from its refusal to…

image.caption: The research vessel was taking a group of researchers to Barentsburg, a Russian coal mining settlement on the Arctic Svalbard archipelagoImage: Sergei Malgavko/TASS/picture alliance

blocks.text: Norwegian courts have ordered the seizure of a Russian ship in the Arctic to enforce part of a $4.22 billion (roughly €3.6 billion) compensation claim won by Ukrainian state energy firm Naftogaz after Moscow's seizure of its assets in Crimea, which Russia illegally annexed in 2014.
Officials announced that the ship had been stopped from departing the port in the Russian coal mining settlement of Barentsburg in the Svalbard archipelago late on Wednesday.
Svalbard has been Norwegian territory since 1925 but is a demilitarized zone where people from dozens of countries, Russia included, can settle without visas under certain conditions.
Russia's ambassador to Norway said that Moscow would pursue the ship's release through legal channels.

blocks.caption: Around two thirds of Svalbard is designated as national parks and nature reserves, but the coal mining settlement of Barentsburg is home to about a tenth of the archipelago's populationImage: Sergei Malgavko/TASS/picture alliance

blocks.text: What do we know about the Professor Molchanov ship being impounded?

The first group to announce the ship's seizure was Covington, the US law firm representing Naftogaz as it tries to secure the compensation awarded to it by the Permanent Court of Arbitration in the Hague in 2023.

Russia had refused to pay the fine plus legal fees and interest amid its ongoing war with Ukraine, and Naftogaz has since begun trying to secure the seizure and forced sale of Russian commercial assets via local courts instead.
"Russia cannot evade ​responsibility simply by refusing to comply with an international arbitral award," said Naftogaz acting CEO Sergii Fedorenko.

Covington said it had been tracking the ship, the Professor Molchanov, for months. It said its application was approved on Monday by the Nord-Troms and Senja District Court, which ordered Svalbard's governor to ensure the ship stayed in dock once it arrived.
The end of coal mining in Svalbard
The Svalbard governor's office later issued a statement confirming that the ship had been seized and would be held in Svalbard.

"The governor will take care of the crew and passengers on board the vessel in collaboration with Trust Arktikugol," it said, referring to the Russian enterprise (meaning "Arctic Coal") that administers the Barentsburg mining settlement.
Norway's Justice Ministry, meanwhile, said the issue did not directly concern the government in Oslo.
"Russia can demand that ​the district court reassess the case," the Justice ‌Ministry said.
How did Russia respond?
Russia's ambassador to Norway, Nikolai Korchunov, said in a statement on Thursday that Moscow would pursue the ship's release through legal channels.
"We insist on the immediate release of the vessel and on ensuring the safety of its passengers and crew," he said.
The Kremlin also summoned Norway's ambassador in Moscow to lodge a formal complaint.
Is Svalbard Russia's real leverage in the Arctic?
The Professor Molchanov, a repurposed research vessel, arrived in Barentsburg on Tuesday with a party of Russian scientists, according to a journalist who was accompanying them.

"The seizure has had no impact on the expedition participants or the ship's crew. No one has been arrested. We are all going about our business as usual," Andrei Gorbunov, editor-in-chief of Komsomolskaya Pravda (KP) radio wrote on KP's website.
He said that for the time being, "the Professor Mochanov is simply forbidden from leaving the port of Barentsburg," adding it was unclear how long this would remain the case.

blocks.caption: Prior to the war in Ukraine Barentsburg was also home to Ukrainian and other foreign nationals. But most have since left, Ukrainians in particular were told to accept an offer of Russian citizenship or leave. Image: Sergei Malgavko/TASS/picture alliance

blocks.text: What is behind Svalbard's special status, and why is it home to the Barentsburg settlement?
Svalbard is an archipelago well to the north of mainland Norway in the Arctic Circle, sparsely populated and thought to be home to slightly fewer than 3,000 people.
It was a whaling base in the 17th and 18th centuries and became a coal mining site at the beginning of the 20th century.

The territory was recognized as part of Norway in 1925, but only after the 1920 establishment of an international treaty — which nowadays has dozens of signatories — designating the area a demilitarized zone where anybody from a signatory state was permitted to settle and work without a visa, provided they met certain conditions.

The Soviet Union eventually acquired three sites and developed them as company towns: Barentsburg, with a remnant population of around 300 mostly Russian nationals, the nearly-abandoned settlement of Pyramiden, and Grumant, which has been left as a ghost town for decades.
Tourism has become a growth industry on the stark but stunning polar archipelago.

articles.title: DFA: 39 diplomatic protests lodged vs. China's actions in WPS in 2026
articles.summary: The Department of Foreign Affairs (DFA) on Thursday reported that it has so far lodged 39 diplomatic protests against China's actions in the West Philippine Sea in 2026.

blocks.text: Published September 3, 2026 11:19pm
The Department of Foreign Affairs (DFA) on Thursday reported that it has so far lodged 39 diplomatic protests against China's actions in the West Philippine Sea in 2026.
DFA spokesperson for maritime affairs Deputy Assistant Secretary Regelio Villanueva Jr. made the report during the agency's budget deliberation at the House of Representatives.
"From 2026 this year, we have already issued 39 protests. And from 2022 to 2026, the total number of diplomatic protests that we have issued stands at 296 already," he added.
When asked about the changes brought by the diplomatic protests, Foreign Affairs Secretary Theresa Lazaro said she observed fewer incidents from China.

"The only change that I can cite right now is that the incidents that have happened in the past, the water cannoning, the laser, I think it has sort of decreased, and therefore these are the significant changes," Lazaro said in the same hearing.
"Although we know very well that our defense establishments have always been citing also the Chinese military vessels," she added.
Villanueva said the DFA is coordinating with the country's security agencies in addressing the issues in the West Philippine Sea.

"We have to understand also that results on the ground may take time because while diplomacy is the bigger tool in the government's toolbox, we have to work in tandem with other government agencies, particularly our security agencies, our National Maritime Council, because this is a whole-of-government effort," Villanueva said.
"So all these things will factor in. This is not to say that we expect to see immediate results because we have to be patient. We have to take time," he added.
On Tuesday, the Armed Forces of the Philippines (AFP) said 56 Chinese vessels have been monitored in some of the West Philippine Sea features in August 2026.
These features are the following:
• Ayungin Shoal – 18 Chinese vessels (17 CCGs one PLAN)• Bajo de Masinloc – 23 (14 CCGs nine PLANs)• Escoda Shoal – nine (five CCGs four PLANs)• Pag-asa Islands – six (five CCGs, one PLAN)
This was higher compared to the 48 Chinese ships seen in the disputed area in July 2026.
Meanwhile, AFP reported that China has yet to compensate the Filipino sailor who lost a finger during a 2024 incident in the West Philippine Sea.
It added that the serviceman received support only from individuals, civil society groups and the private sector in the Philippines following the incident.

On June 17, 2024, Philippine Navy Seaman First Class Underwater Operator Jeffrey Facundo lost his right thumb after China vessels collided with Philippine boats while the AFP was conducting a rotation and resupply mission to the BRP Sierra Madre at Ayungin Shoal. —LDF, GMA News

articles.title: Germany: From emigration to immigration destination
articles.summary: Migration is a sensitive topic in Germany, with public debate dominated by the fear of uncontrolled immigration. People forget that, over two centuries, millions of Germans emigrated in search of a…

image.caption: A statue in the port of Bremerhaven commemorates the millions of Germans who emigrated abroadImage: S. Ziese/blickwinkel/picture alliance

blocks.text: "Why should [they] be suffered to swarm into our Settlements, and by herding together establish their Language and Manners to the Exclusion of ours? [...] [They] will shortly be so numerous [...] and will never adopt our Language or Customs."

These defamatory comments about refugees and asylum-seekers sound as if they might have been made today by the right-wing populist Alternative for Germany party (AfD). Yet in this instance, the people vilified and accused of refusing to integrate are Germans — and the harsh judgement was made in the 18th century by none other than Benjamin Franklin, one of the Founding Fathers of the United States.

The pursuit of happiness and a better life are mentioned in the American Declaration of Independence, which Franklin helped write. Over the centuries, they have been the motivation for countless people to turn their backs on their respective homelands.

blocks.caption: Benjamin Franklin, one of the Founding Fathers of the United States, warned against accepting German immigrantsImage: Public Domain

blocks.text: The Germans who emigrated to America in Franklin's lifetime were actually fairly limited in number. By 1820, only about 150,000 had successfully made the journey. Often, they were persuaded by compatriots who told tales of their tremendous success in their new homeland and celebrated the prosperity they had supposedly attained in a very short space of time. What most people back home didn't know was that these recruiters received a commission for every migrant.

"The crossing on a sailing ship cost about what a tradesman would earn in a year," said Simone Blaschka of the German Emigration Center in Bremerhaven. "To be able to afford that, families had to sell all their worldly goods."
A journey into the unknown

They would have had no idea what awaited them on board the ship. During the crossing, which took several weeks, they were packed together below deck in a very confined space, plagued by bedbugs, fleas and rats. Many fell sick with dysentery, typhoid, smallpox or scurvy.

In his book "Journey to Pennsylvania in the Year 1750," the schoolmaster and organist Gottlieb Mittelberger described what he had experienced on the voyage: "Many people whimper, sigh and cry piteously for their homes; most of them get home-sick. Many hundred people necessarily die and perish in such misery, and must be cast into the sea."

blocks.caption: Many European immigrants who came to the US in the 20th century arrived by boat in New YorkImage: Raimund Franken/imageBROKER/picture alliance

blocks.text: On arrival in America, Mittelberger wrote, the majority of his fellow passengers were effectively auctioned off. These were people without means who were granted free passage after undertaking to work for years as bonded laborers in exchange. In the US, their contracts were sold off. Mittelberger saw families torn apart and parents forced to sell their children.
An invitation from Russia

As these early migrants were traveling to America, there was simultaneously a big wave of emigration from Germany to the east. People followed the call of the Russian czarina, Catherine the Great, herself a German princess by birth.

On July 22, 1763, she issued a manifesto inviting people to come to Russia, with the aim of cultivating uninhabited regions for arable farming. She promised the new arrivals free transport to their chosen place of residence, land, also free of charge, the first year tax-free, schooling, exemption from military service, and a special political status that would allow them to maintain the German language and, for the most part, govern themselves.

blocks.caption: Catherine the Great officially invited Germans to immigrate to Russia in the late 18th centuryImage: akg-images/picture-alliance

blocks.text: However, in the 19th century the American continent once again became the dream destination. "The German population almost doubled in the 19th century, so you can imagine what the job market was like," said Blaschka from the German Emigration Center. The situation was exacerbated by failed harvests and famines.
"People didn't see any future for themselves or their children, and decided to emigrate," she said. In this way, around 6 million Germans were drawn to the New World.
Migration: A burden or an asset?
Germans were far from the only ones who left their homeland.

"Between the beginning of the 19th century and the World War I, there were probably around 60 million Europeans who left their homes," said Jochen Oltmer, a professor at the Institute for Migration Research and Intercultural Studies in Osnabrück. Then, in the mid-20th century, this trend reversed and Europe went from being a continent of emigration to one of immigration.

blocks.caption: Migration researcher Jochen Oltmer has studied the immigration waves to and from Europe in the 19th and 20th centuriesImage: Michael Gründel/NOZ

blocks.text: In the 1950s and '60s, the future looked rosy for postwar West Germany and its "economic miracle." From 1956 onward, so-called "guest worker trains" arrived in stations like Stuttgart, Dortmund and Cologne, carrying Italians, Greeks, Spaniards, Portuguese, Yugoslavs and Turks, attracted by the promise of well-paid jobs in the new Federal Republic.
By the time the ban on recruiting foreign labor came into force in 1973, around 14 million people had come to West Germany as "guest workers." Around 3 million stayed permanently.

Yet Germany still did not consider itself an immigration country. "For a very long time, we were dealing with the mindset: It doesn't matter why people came to the Federal Republic; they don't belong, because in any case they'll leave the country again and disappear," said Oltmer.

blocks.caption: Between 1956 and 1973, around 14 million 'guest workers' came to Germany from other European countriesImage: Hans Heckmann/dpa/picture alliance

blocks.text: In 2025, according to Germany's Federal Statistical Office, more than 30% of Germany's total population had a migrant background. Yet many third- and fourth-generation citizens still don't feel they belong, which has to do with the perspective of the society in which they live.
Who's welcome – and who isn't?
These days, Germany is keen to attract skilled workers, but refugees are only granted asylum if they are politically persecuted in their homeland, or are fleeing war.

As a migration researcher, Oltmer is constantly examining the reasons why some migrants are accepted and others are not. This question was especially relevant in 2015, when refugees came to Germany in very large numbers.

"The attitude was: 'OK, you people from Syria, in light of the Syrian civil war, you are entitled to protection.' But at the same time this society says of people from Afghanistan, 'In your case, we're a bit more sceptical,'" he said.

blocks.caption: Germany took in hundreds of thousands of refugees in 2015, above all people fleeing the civil war in SyriaImage: Johannes Simon/Getty Images

blocks.text: Yet asylum accounts for barely 10% of immigration to Germany, Oltmer explained. The majority of immigrants are not people fleeing their country. "This means that when it comes to scandalization and the creation of certain negative images, we are seeing a massive distortion of the debate." And the descendants of the German emigrants Benjamin Franklin once reviled as "Palatine boors" have long since perfectly integrated into American society.

In Germany, however, integration is taking much longer. "Many people have no possibility of regularizing their status and obtaining a stable residence permit, even though everyone involved knows they can stay, and will stay," said Oltmer. He believes people urgently need to sit down and clarify how they want German society to look in future.
"It may be a very hard, even hurtful discussion. But it's the only way."
Berlin initiative helps immigrant moms find their feet
This article was originally written in German.

articles.title: Ombudsman urges examination of judiciary; SC says file proper complaints
articles.summary: Ombudsman Jesus Crispin "Boying" Remulla on Thursday said the judiciary should be examined closely by those in government, and its members should do some soul-searching after magistrates reversed…

blocks.text: Ombudsman Jesus Crispin "Boying" Remulla on Thursday said the judiciary should be examined closely by those in government, and its members should do some soul-searching after magistrates reversed rulings by his office and by the Department of Justice when he was its secretary.

The Supreme Court hours later issued a statement, inviting the Ombudsman to file the proper complaints and submit evidence so that the High Tribunal can "determine the facts and, when warranted, exercise its disciplinary authority."

At a hearing on the P7.2-billion budget proposed under the National Expenditure Program, Remulla expressed his frustration over reversals by the Court of Appeals. He cited a CA ruling that reversed the dismissal of some barangay chairpersons.
"That is a trend, your honor, that is known to the Office of the Ombudsman. It's something that I spoke about to Senior Associate Justice Marvic Leonen," Remulla told senators.

"I told him about this problem that we have. Because institutionally, it's very discouraging to be conducting all of these activities only to be reversed by the Court of Appeals decision that came out of nowhere,” he added.

Leonen was Remulla’s classmate at the University of the Philippines College of Law. Remulla said that his batchmate has already cautioned him in the past for his strong remarks, but he wanted to be direct.

Remulla cited an incident when he was still the secretary of the Department of Justice (DOJ). The Office of the Ombudsman had dismissed someone from the National Bureau of Investigation, only for the CA to later reinstate the person.
The Ombudsman called such trends discouraging.

“As a lawyer, it’s not really common for lawyers to complain about the courts. But sometimes, we just have to raise that issue already because it can be the biggest elephant in the room, within our justice system,” Remulla said.

“It’s the biggest elephant in the room. The judiciary has to be examined closely by everybody in government, and they themselves should go on a soul-searching, so that we can be a better country. I think that is one of the problems besetting us right now,” he added.
Remulla said that for all the EDSA revolutions that the country has experienced, the judicial branch has not yet been touched.
“Never has the judiciary accounted for everything that they’ve been doing. It is something that we have to examine as a country,” Remulla said.

Remulla said that there was a Justice Sector Coordinating Council which gathered courts, the DOJ, and the Department of Interior and Local Government, which had been funded by the European Union. The Office of the Ombudsman could be included in the council to streamline efforts, he said.
The SC responded to Remulla’s statements, saying it takes such accusations seriously if the proper processes are followed.
In a statement, the High Tribunal asked the Ombudsman to file the proper complaints and present evidence.

“The Court cannot act on broad allegations against an entire appellate court based only on public statements. We therefore invite the Ombudsman, or any concerned party, to file the proper complaint and submit supporting evidence," the SC said.
"This will allow the Court to determine the facts and, when warranted, exercise its disciplinary authority,” it added.

The SC also cited the case of Heydarian, Cendaña, and Gadon. In that case, the SC struck down cases that sought to hold Presidential Adviser for Poverty Alleviation Larry Gadon, Akbayan party-list Rep. Percival Cendaña, and political analyst Richard Heydarian in contempt over their remarks on the dismissal of the impeachment raps against Vice President Sara Duterte in 2025.
“Despite the strong statements made against the Court concerning one of its rulings, the Court upheld the respondents’ freedom of speech and did not hold them in contempt," the SC said.

"The Court welcomes fair criticism. At the same time, serious accusations against judges and courts should be raised through the proper processes so they can be fairly investigated and resolved,” it added. —NB, GMA News

articles.title: EU’s ability to defend against invasion remains in doubt, finds official report
articles.summary: Fragmented infrastructure and reliance on US continue to hinder ‘defence readiness’, says European court of auditors

blocks.text: The EU’s ability to respond to a foreign invasion by 2030 remains in doubt due to a continuing reliance on the US and fragmented national defence systems, according to a report from its official auditor.

The European court of auditors (ECA) said the EU was much better prepared than before Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine of 2022, but achieving its goal of defence readiness by the end of the decade would be difficult.

“Achieving defence preparedness in the EU by 2030 remains challenging,” said Marek Opioła, an ECA member who led the review of the EU’s defence policy published on Thursday. “There are still major difficulties such as fragmented national systems or industrial bottlenecks. We also still rely on the United States.”
Speaking to the Guardian, he stressed the EU could “still make major progress” if it sharply increased defence spending and rapidly expanded ammunition production.

Between 2020 and 2025, EU member states increased defence spending by 79%, a response to the Russian threat and a belated effort to meet Nato spending targets. In November 2024, the EU met its pledge of providing 1 million rounds of ammunition to Ukraine – eight months behind schedule.
The EU set the goal of defence readiness by 2030 last year, after intelligence services warned that Russia could be ready to wage a large-scale war in Europe around that time.

The bloc’s financial watchdog said major difficulties had to be overcome to reach this target, defined by a senior auditor as “having strategic autonomy” and “the ability to independently sustain high-intensity warfare”. The senior auditor said the EU was better prepared than 2019 when a similar review was conducted, but warned that fragmented national defence industries and “insufficient cooperation” between EU governments contributed to a risk of duplication in spending or persistent gaps in military capabilities.

Emblematic of the dysfunction – although not mentioned in the report – is France and Germany’s decision to abandon a €100bn project to build a joint fighter jet, because the lead companies were unable to resolve disputes over leadership and control.

The report highlighted a possible tension between short-term battlefield needs and a “Buy European” policy that aims to reduce dependencies on foreign suppliers. Between February 2022 and June 2023, 78% of EU governments’ defence acquisitions were sourced outside the bloc, with the US alone representing 63%, according to one study cited by the ECA.

The senior auditor said purchases from the US went up after Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine “which was understandable because the EU needed to find capabilities that were available quickly”. The official added that “early signs of improvement in that situation” were visible, although the auditors did not have complete data to draw conclusions.
after newsletter promotion

The EU has set requirements that common defence spending should benefit domestic defence industries or those of closely-associated countries, such as Ukraine and Norway. But some flexibilities have been allowed where Europe is unable to produce critical supplies in time.

After a brutal summer of deadly Russian missile and drone attacks, this week Ukraine asked for an exemption from Buy European procurement rules to acquire US-made Patriot interceptors using the EU’s €90bn support loan. The European Commission president, Ursula von der Leyen, said on Wednesday that Ukraine had requested funding “worth several billion euros” for air defences, including Patriot air-defence systems. A commission spokesperson said Ukraine’s request for Patriot interceptor missiles “would require a derogation” from rules requiring majority European content in military purchases under the loan. “The final say is with the member states and of course our hope would be that this would soon be granted,” the spokesperson said.

The senior auditor said sometimes “it may make sense” to buy outside “when you have a short-term urgent need”. The person added: “Even if you buy something that you don’t have in-house, you [should] always have a plan how to develop that critical capacity in the long-term within the European Union.”

articles.title: BoM forecasts strongest El Niño on record as research points to ‘alarming’ climate change influence
articles.summary: Bureau of Meteorology suggests El Niño has already broken records, with Pacific ocean temperature change exceeding 2C in six months
articles.byline: Graham Readfearn Environment and climate correspondent

blocks.text: The growing El Niño weather phenomenon to Australia’s east is already breaking heat records, with forecasts showing it will likely easily surpass previous events, according to Australia’s Bureau of Meteorology, as seperate research suggested climate change had greatly shortened the odds of the event hitting record extremes.

On Thursday the UN’s weather agency said the event in the Pacific was continuing to strengthen and would probably persist until early 2027, warning it had the “potential to deliver a massive blow to communities and economies across the world”.

The UN secretary general, António Guterres, said: “El Niño is being supersized before our eyes. The science leaves no room for doubt: the planet is in uncharted waters, and those waters are heating up.”

In an update this week, the Bureau of Meteorology said the El Niño was now forecast to peak in late spring or summer and “reach levels above the warmest observed since reliable records began in 1950”.
El Niño events tend to mean hotter and drier conditions for Australia’s south and east in winter and spring, and can increase the risk of heatwaves, drought and bushfires.

El Niño strength is assessed by analysing sea surface temperatures in a region of the equatorial Pacific known as Niño 3.4. The bureau has said the strength of an El Niño does not necessarily mean stronger effects for the continent.
However, bureau analysis of the unfolding event suggested this El Niño had already broken records.

“We have been looking at the rate of warming observed in the last two months and it has been faster than any other event. Not only is it strong, but it has escalated rapidly,” said Felicity Gamble, a senior climatologist at the BoM.

Gamble said the relative sea surface temperatures in the Niño 3.4 region for the month of August were likely to be between 2.2C and 2.3C above average – higher than any previous August since 1950 (the year after which records are considered to be more reliable).
She said forecasts were suggesting relative sea surface temperatures in that region could peak over 3C above average, compared to the highest previous figure of 2.6C observed in January 1983.
Gamble said the relative sea surface temperatures in the Niño 3.4 region had warmed by more than 2C between February and July.
She said: “No other period in the historical record exceeds that. This is the first event where we have had that change exceed 2C in the space of six months.
“We could be seeing a record in terms of the strength, and also the rate of warming and the duration.”
after newsletter promotion
Climate experts have said El Niño will likely combine with climate change to push global temperatures to record highs next year.
Gamble said in the Pacific region, El Niño was already contributing to droughts in Papua New Guinea, with food and water shortages and major wildfires in Indonesia.
This winter was Australia’s third-warmest on record and the hottest on record for New South Wales, Tasmania and Victoria.

Scientists at the University of Melbourne have released preliminary research into the influence of climate change on the predicted peak of the El Niño. By analysing historical records and comparing climate models with and without the influence of greenhouse gas emissions, the scientists found climate change had made “an event of this magnitude” six times more likely.
The study has been submitted to a journal for peer review, but the authors said they had used a methodology common to many other published studies.

Dr Andrew King, one of the co-authors of the research, said: “This points to the fact that there is likely a climate change role here in the chance of having these extreme El Niño conditions. It seems likely there is a human fingerprint emerging in this event.
“We are seeing something that does not appear to have happened before and that is alarming.”

The bureau’s long range forecast for September to November points to an increased chance of below average rainfall for the south and east, but above average for most of the continent’s western half. Temperatures are also likely to be above average south of the tropics.

articles.title: US commerce secretary erroneously said no Americans have died in Iran war, Trump claims
articles.summary:
President said Howard Lutnick had Venezuela operation on his mind when he was discussing Iran war on CNBC

Donald Trump has claimed his commerce secretary, Howard Lutnick, erroneously stated…

blocks.text: Donald Trump has claimed his commerce secretary, Howard Lutnick, erroneously stated that no Americans had been killed in the war with Iran because he was thinking about a previous US operation, in Venezuela.
The claim, at odds with the Pentagon’s count of 18 US service members dead in the US-Israel war on Iran, sparked a swift backlash as Trump struggles to end the conflict after six months.
In a post on his Truth Social platform on Thursday, the US president wrote: “Sec. Lutnick had Venezuela on his mind when he said nobody was killed. 18 people were killed in Iran!”

The rebuke came a day after Lutnick appeared on CNBC’s Squawk Box and framed the Trump administration’s approach to Iran as primarily economic. Describing the strategy as an “economic choke-out”, he erroneously told the network there had not been American deaths in the conflict, adding that he was optimistic bond markets would respond well to the approach.

Lutnick this morning acknowledged the mistake, posting on X that he had misspoken and also claiming he had been thinking of the US operation in Venezuela, where US forces captured Nicolás Maduro in January with minimal US casualties. The Pentagon said seven US troops were injured and none were killed in that operation, while Venezuelan officials put their overall death toll at 47, and Cuba said 32 of its military and police personnel were killed.

Trump’s post landed as Iranian authorities detailed heavy casualties from the latest US strikes. Iran’s health ministry said Tuesday night’s strikes killed 18 people and wounded 108, while the country’s Red Crescent identified that four people were killed and 67 wounded when a US strike hit a wedding ceremony near the coast of the strait of Hormuz, which also killed a child. Reuters said it was able to verify the location of the damaged building using satellite imagery.
A US Central Command spokesperson, Capt Tim Hawkins, said the US military does not target civilians and that the reports, which originated with Iranian state media, were being reviewed.

The strikes were part of a broader operation that Central Command said hit Iranian air defense systems, radar installations, maritime assets, mine-laying equipment and communications sites near the strait of Hormuz, a strategic waterway through which a large share of the world’s oil passes.

The Pentagon’s capacity to independently verify such claims has been sharply reduced. Its Civilian Protection Center of Excellence has been cut from 40 staff to nine since the start of last year, according to the Pentagon’s own inspector general, while the department has also stopped developing a database meant to track civilian harm from US operations.
The episode has exposed a wider tension in how the White House is presenting the conflict.

Officials have sought to characterize the campaign (estimated to have cost at least $37.5bn as of July) against Iran in economic terms even as it continues to produce US military deaths, mounting Iranian civilian casualties and rising oil prices.
Polling from UMass-Amherst in late August found that 54% of Americans disapprove of the war initiated by the US and Israel, and one in six Trump voters would go back and change their vote in 2024.

The current round of fighting began after the US struck rocket launchers on Larak Island that officials said were being prepared to mine the strait, prompting Iranian missile and drone attacks on US and allied positions in Jordan, Bahrain, Kuwait and Iraq. Jordanian authorities said 13 ballistic missiles were fired at the country, of which 10 were intercepted.

Trump described Iran’s retaliation as a “love tap”, but warned that further strikes remained an option. “It was a very heavy attack last night, and we’re prepared to do another one anytime we want,” he said earlier this week.

articles.title: COA flags gaps in confidential fund rules, says multiple SDOs allowed
articles.summary: The Commission on Audit (COA) said it is looking to revisit rules governing confidential and intelligence funds, including the use of aliases, documentation for informants, and the requirements for…

blocks.text: The Commission on Audit (COA) said it is looking to revisit rules governing confidential and intelligence funds, including the use of aliases, documentation for informants, and the requirements for paying rewards, as senators pressed the audit body on safeguards for the disbursement and liquidation of such funds.
During the Senate hearing on COA’s proposed 2027 budget, COA chairperson Gamaliel Cordoba said the existing joint memorandum circular has provisions that need to be reviewed and clarified.

The rules are contained in Joint Circular No. 2015-01, issued by COA, the Department of Budget and Management, the Department of the Interior and Local Government, the Governance Commission for GOCCs and the Department of National Defense. The circular governs the entitlement, release, use, reporting and audit of confidential and intelligence funds.
During the hearing, COA officials clarified that an agency may designate more than one special disbursing officer (SDO) to handle confidential or intelligence funds.

An SDO is responsible for making the disbursements and maintaining the required records for the funds. Under the current rules, cash advances for confidential funds are drawn by duly designated and bonded SDOs or by the head of agency, upon approval of the agency head.
Cordoba said there is no prescribed limit on the number of SDOs an agency may designate.
“Nasa head of agency o ahensya ang pamamaraan kung sino ang assigned SDO,” he said.
(It is up to the head of the agency to determine who will be assigned as SDO.)
The official explained that an agency may have different SDOs for different programs, provided they meet the requirements for accountable officers, including proper bonding and accountability.
“Basta ang SDO can be multiple, there is no limit as long as proper management and proper bonding and accountability can be had,” the official noted.
(There can be multiple SDOs; there is no limit as long as there is proper management, bonding and accountability.)
Under the existing circular, the SDO must maintain separate records of transactions, prepare liquidation and progress reports, and submit the required documents to COA.
COA wants clearer rules on aliases
The discussion also turned to the use of aliases or code names in documents supporting confidential-fund transactions.

He said the existing joint circular does not clearly settle the issue and that COA has identified the use of aliases and the identities appearing in acknowledgment receipts as areas requiring further review.

The concern has also surfaced in recent Senate proceedings, where a former COA auditor testified that Joint Circular No. 2015-01 is silent on whether aliases may be used in documents supporting confidential-fund disbursements.
Cordoba added that the proposed review would look at how identities can be protected without compromising COA’s ability to properly audit the use of public funds.
He said there should be a way for auditors with the appropriate clearance to verify identities where necessary while preserving the confidentiality of intelligence operations and informants.
Proof required for rewards
COA also emphasized that payment for information and payment of rewards are not the same thing.

An official explained that an agency may pay for information as part of a confidential operation, but a reward carries an additional requirement: there must be evidence showing that the information or surveillance activity resulted in a successful outcome.
“Pag-reward ang pinag-usapan natin kakaiba, pag sinabi nating reward may kaakibat na success,” Cordoba noted.
(When we are talking about a reward, it is different; a reward carries with it the requirement of success.)
The official said the rules require documentation showing the success of the information-gathering or surveillance activity.
Possible evidence could include records of an arrest or other documents demonstrating that the information provided led to a concrete result.
“Importante ang dokumento,” the official added.
(The documentation is important.)

The official also added that simply presenting an acknowledgment receipt would not, by itself, establish the success required for a reward. Meanwhile, after two hours of deliberation, the Senate Committee on Finance on Thursday approved the Commission on Audit’s (COA) proposed P16.046-billion budget for 2027.—LDF, GMA News

articles.title: Iran targets US bases as Israel warns sanctions could drive Tehran to ‘desperate steps’
articles.summary:
Air bases used by US in the UAE and Kuwait hit as the Israeli defence chief says Iran’s regime fears collapse due to economic pressures

Iran has continued to demonstrate an ability to target…

blocks.text: Iran has continued to demonstrate an ability to target bases in the Gulf used by the US despite six months of war and a new sanctions regime described by the Trump administration as an “economic D-day”.

As Iran’s military targeted US bases in the United Arab Emirates and Kuwait, despite threats of further strikes by the US president, Israel’s defence chief warned that economic pressures from the sanctions could lead Tehran to escalate to more “extreme measures”.

“This morning, the army hit the satellite communication systems, equipment depots and fighter aircraft hangars of the terrorist US army at the Ahmad al-Jaber air base in Kuwait with missiles and drones,” the Iranian military said on Thursday in a statement carried by state television.
The “location of forces and radar systems of the child-killing US army at the Al Minhad air base in the UAE were also attacked by missiles and drones of the army”, it added.
In a post on X, Kuwait’s ministry of defence said its air defences had intercepted missile and drone attacks during a “blatant Iranian aggression”.
The Kuwaiti statement came after the US allies Bahrain and Jordan said their air defence systems intercepted several Iranian air attacks on Wednesday.

Fighting between the US and Iran has increased this week after the US hit Iranian rocket launchers on an island in the strait of Hormuz on Sunday, claiming that Iran was planning to use them to shoot mines into the waterway.

The latest flare-up in the conflict comes amid little evidence that the Trump administration is succeeding in advancing its nebulous war aims either on the battlefield or via mediation, despite the US president’s repeated claims to have opened the strait of Hormuz to oil traffic.

Instead, traffic through the key maritime passageway remains far below prewar levels, with oil prices remaining stubbornly elevated ahead of US midterm elections. Oil prices jumped again on Thursday after the Iranian strikes.

Among the weapons Iran has used this week is its Kheibar Shekan medium-range ballistic missile system. The cheap and accurate missile can be launched within minutes and has become a staple of Iranian strikes.

The rocket’s solid fuel motor means it does not require lengthy fuelling. It can be deployed very quickly to avoid detection and can be armed with a powered and steerable final stage to help beat anti-missile systems.

Despite claims by the Trump administration that Tehran is running out of rockets, Iran continues to fire missiles that are considerably cheaper to produce than the US interceptors used to shoot them down.
Iran has claimed as recently as the end of August that it maintained both missiles stockpiles and the ability to manufacture them.

“Initially, some believed that Iran had only a limited number of missiles and that its stockpiles would eventually be depleted as the war continued,” the IRGC spokesperson Brig Gen Hossein Mohebbi said.

“However, that assumption proved incorrect, as Iran’s missile capability has remained sustained and its missile production has continued.” Mohebbi’s characterisation of Iranian missile stockpiles could not be verified.

The continued strikes came as Israel’s defence minister, Israel Katz, said that while the new US economic sanctions appeared to be effective, the increased pressure might lead Tehran into extreme measures.

“We see signs indicating that the heavy economic pressure they are under, and the fear of an uprising and the collapse of the regime, may push them to desperate steps,” Katz said at a ceremony for defence ministry employees.
The hawkish minister reiterated the threats against the Islamic Republic that he has made in recent months.

“An Iranian attack on Israel will free Israel from any existing constraint,” he said. “We will strike all of Iran’s national military and civilian infrastructure – including energy infrastructure – and push Iran deep back into the stone age.”

articles.title: Putin denies fresh mobilization campaign in Ukraine war
articles.summary: The Russian president said there was no present need to mobilize more men, describing the reports as Ukrainian "disinformation." Putin was speaking during an economic forum in Russia's east.

image.caption: Putin said he was grateful to countries which were making an effort to mediate a resolution to the conflictImage: Vyacheslav Prokofyev/Sputnik/AP Photo/picture alliance

blocks.text: Russia is not preparing to mobilize more men to fight, President Vladimir Putin on Thursday, describing such speculation as Ukrainian "disinformation."
In 2022 and a few months after Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine, Putin ordered the unpopular "partial mobilization" of reservists amid a string of military set backs.
The decision prompted an exodus of draft-age men from Russia and the Kremlin has since repeatedly denied plans for another mobilization.
"There is no scenario today that would require mobilization," Putin told a plenary session of the Eastern Economic Forum in Vladivostok.

"This is a disinformation campaign by the enemy in the run-up to the State Duma elections, aimed at influencing the outcome," he added, referring to Russian parliamentary elections later this month. "As is well known, our people enlist voluntarily and sign a contract."
Putin had already dismissed mobilization speculations earlier this week, calling such reports "utter nonsense" and an "information attack" against Russia.
What did Putin say about peace in Ukraine?
Putin once again claimed there was a chance for peace with Ukraine, but stressed the conflict must be resolved by Moscow and Kyiv.
His statements come amid intensified Russian attacks on the Ukrainian capital. Meanwhile, Kyiv has intensified its attacks deeper within Russia, striking online retailers and other civilian targets.
Russia launches missile and drone barrage on Kyiv
Putin thanked countries which were making an effort to mediate a resolution to the conflict. He said the US and China, among others, were ready to support a peace settlement.

"Ultimately, however, the problem must be resolved ​by the countries involved in the conflict — Russia and Ukraine. ⁠This ​is the correct ​approach. Yet, we are grateful ​to everyone attempting to ‌ contribute to a settlement. Is there ​a ⁠chance? In my view, yes, there is," Putin said.

Still, he went on to condemn Ukraine, saying warnings about risks to planes in Russian airspace amount to "state terrorism." On Tuesday, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy warned that his country's drones have made Russian airspace unsafe for planes.

blocks.caption: Putin was speaking during the Eastern Economic Forum in VladivostokImage: Vyacheslav Prokofyev/AFP

blocks.text: How has Moscow responded to Zelenskyy's airspace warning?
On Thursday, Russia's Transport Ministry said it has provided clarifications to foreign airlines about Russian airports' and airspace safety measures.
"They work very closely with us and ​understand all our rules, standards and how we ​ensure flight safety," Russian news agency Interfax ​quoted ‌Transport Minister Andrei Nikitin as saying.
He added that the clarifications were given in response to requests from foreign carriers.

On Wednesday, Russian aviation watchdog Rosaviatsiya stressed in a statement that the country's "air transport, its ground infrastructure, continue to operate ​normally, receiving and dispatching flights, including those of foreign airlines."
European and US carriers have avoided Russian airspace since Moscow launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022. However, other airlines from China, Turkey and the Gulf states still use it.
Could deadly strikes inside Russia backfire on Ukraine?
